description:
Creating the world's most innovative nebulous Earth jukebox

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earth
summary: We developed an Earth jukebox sonification web app, with our own jukebox audio player design, that can take data in the form of equirectangular images (e.g. https://svs.gsfc.nasa.gov/3912/ ) and produce notes by taking the average RGB values for each vertical image slice, allowing the user to understand data in an auditory way!
details:
We built an audio player and sonification processing web app in the style of an old-school jukebox, with the aim of mixing our team's artistic abilities with our technical skills, to make an ejoyable and easy-to-use way to interpret scientific Earth data maps.

How it works
You can select one of the selected NASA Earth data maps we source from NASA's Scientific Visualization Studio or upload your own into the UI.
Then, we run it through several functions:
1. We split the image into vertical chunks (e.g. 160 chunks).
2. For each chunk, we find the average RGB values, its hue and its brightness.
3. We identify if it has usable data (i.e. not fully black, white or gray) by finding the different between the highest and lowest R, G, or B value - if it's within a threshold this gets skipped as unusable.
4. If it passes those checks, we determine a frequency using the brightness and hue of the chunk, and factor in any user settings like the wave form, to generate a tone using the Web Audio API. We also added more complex modes to interpret data differently: generating a chord or an arpeggio from this visual data.
5. Once generated, the user can use the audio controls to play the tune and interact with it by changing its settings to get interesting sounds!

Benefits and Impact
We included a short description of each of the data sets in the browse page to help people learn what they are, and we hope this project inspires people to creatively use data. Without interpretation, data has no meaning, so we plan to use to this tool to make this colour dat into useful information which could feed into our own music creation or explore data in a way that doesn't depend on visual representation!

Tools and Resources
We used many tools we were familiar with from our own projects! This includes: Vue.js, Node.js, Three.js (3D for web), Web Audio API (for sound), Gemini for researching our tool stack most applicable, and some small open-source LLMs to help generate a code skeleton to save time! We used tools like Inkscape for digital design, Draw.io for wireframing, and font and icon libraries like Phosphor Icons and Google Fonts. We used GitHub to host our code, and deployed it live to share it with the world and our friends & family using Netlify.

Why our project is creative
The greatest strength of our project is the custom hand-made visuals which make it friendly for a beginner or a younger audience to try out the tool, and the customisability - we added lots of configurable values for the sonification to ensure the user's creatiity for using the tool is not bound, so we added pitch shifting, reverb, adjusting the length/seconds per each note, several chord/arpeggio/single note modes. We also have many export options as we hope people can make fun audio projects by processing their data images on the site and exporting as WAV/MP4/MIDI! (We also included an Easter egg of a Disco mode and a Mythology mode of Atlas holding the Earth (jukebox) to make playing your audio even more fun!).

Factors considered
When ideating, we considered many options: whether to go down the route of scientific visualisations, make a game, or maybe tell a story related to some of the other challenges. We eventually landed on a good middleground of a fun sound-related web project, targeted towards a younger audience or someone looking for a lighthearted web tool for sonification of images, which tied together one of our team member's music production knowledge with the others' product design and software development experiences.

Finally, we hope the fun we had creating the project comes through in the final result, and it was a great opportunity to work with a team and apply our mixed disciplinary skills!
